Emma — thanks for the clear list and the workbook; helpful. High-level answers below and then next steps.

1) Fee phasing: the per-token rates in OF v3 are tiered by cumulative commit over the 12-month period. In practice we invoice against the actual usage at month-end, but discounts tier in once cumulative thresholds are reached. That means the effective per-token price on an invoice can shift retroactively if a threshold is crossed mid-quarter — we'll include a reconciliation line on the following invoice. Im flagging for Kimberly on the legal wording so the reconciliation mechanics are explicit.

2) Invoicing cadence: Redwood issues monthly invoices (in arrears) and will provide a quarterly reconciliation report that shows commit attainment and any credit/debit adjustments. Payment terms are NET45 from invoice date unless you request NET30 and we agree in the order form. Ben, can you confirm standard practice on how we present the monthly + quarterly reconciliation on the invoicing template?

3) VAT/tax allocation: Redwood collects VAT where required; however for certain EU customer setups we support a customer-self-assessed VAT flow (reverse charge). Kimberly will advise on typical redline language and evidence we can provide (VAT registration copy, supplier tax form).

Next steps: Kimberly will send redline suggestions for OF v3 focusing on (a) reconciliation language for tiered pricing, (b) explicit invoicing cadence and payment-term callouts, and (c) VAT allocation options. Ill hold a 30-minute slot on Thursday for a joint call; propose Thu 10/22 9:00–9:30am BST (2:00–2:30am PT) — if thats not workable we can find another slot.

Attachments: none on this message.

Mina / Ben — I reviewed Emmas workbook and drafted redlines against OF v3. Key commercial/legal points in the attached draft (Redwood_OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx):

- Pricing reconciliation: Insert a clause that states we will invoice monthly based on measured usage and apply any tiered discount reconciliation as a single adjustment on the first invoice following the quarter in which the threshold was achieved. The adjustment language must reference the committed quantity schedule in Appendix A to avoid ambiguity.

- Retroactive credits: Limit customer credits to the amount of overpayment for the applicable billing period; exclude punitive interest except where required by law.

- Invoicing & payment terms: Keep NET45 as default for standard customers; allow customers to request NET30 subject to revenue team approval and an explicit line on the Order Form. Also include an example invoice flow in Appendix B so accounting can reconcile PO vs invoice.

- VAT and reverse charge: Provide two selectable checkboxes in the Order Form: (i) Redwood to charge and remit VAT (Redwoods default); (ii) Customer to self-assess under reverse-charge (customer must provide valid VAT registration and indemnity). If customer selects (ii), require submission of VAT registration and a signed tax form prior to first invoice.

- Evidence and timing: For customers electing reverse-charge, add a 10-business-day processing window after Redwood receives VAT evidence before the first invoice reflecting reverse-charge is issued. This reduces back-and-forth on the tax side.

Ben: please review the proposed reconciliation mechanic — specifically how we record the adjustment line so its easy for accounting to handle with our billing system. I added comments where the finance team will need to confirm GL mappings.

Ive attached the redlined doc. Happy to hop on the call with Emma and Paul on Thursday; please confirm the slot and Ill include a brief agenda.

-Kim
